paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God gives second chances, and He does it on purpose. Moses broke the first tablets, and the LORD still said, "Chisel out two stone tablets like the originals, and I will write on them the words that were on the first tablets" (Exodus 34:1). When He describes Himself, He says He is "compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, abounding in loving devotion and faithfulness" (Exodus 34:6). I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, so trust me, a God who comes back for what's broken is the best news I know.

But watch what else the LORD says about Himself. He forgives "iniquity, transgression, and sin," and He also says He "will by no means leave the guilty unpunished" (Exodus 34:7). Mercy and seriousness sit side by side in the same breath. That's why the warnings come right after: no treaties, no other gods, no molten gods, because "the LORD, whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God" (Exodus 34:14, 17). Being forgiven is not a reason to wander off again. It's a reason to stay close.

And look at Moses coming down the mountain. His face was radiant "from speaking with the LORD," and he was unaware of it (Exodus 34:29). Time with God changes you, friend, and sometimes everybody notices before you do. So keep showing up in the Word, keep coming back to Him, and let Him do the shining. The story isn't over, because the LORD who renewed this covenant has more to say.
